verses.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed the lake, and came to his own town.
Some people brought him a paralyzed man lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, he told the man, “Take heart, son. Your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is insulting God.”
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or, ‘Get up and walk’?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” Then he said to the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man got up and went home.
When the crowds saw this, they were amazed and gave glory to God for giving such authority to people.
As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office. “Follow me,” Jesus told him. Matthew got up and followed him.
Later, while Jesus was eating in a house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with him and his disciples.
When the Pharisees saw this, they asked his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard them and said, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do.
Go and learn what this means: ‘I want mercy, not sacrifice.’ I didn’t come to call righteous people; I came to call sinners to turn back to God.”
Then John’s disciples came and asked him, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”
Jesus answered, “Can wedding guests mourn while the groom is with them? The time will come when the groom is taken away from them, and then they’ll fast.
“No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. The patch will pull away from it, and the tear will become worse.
People don’t pour new wine into old wineskins. The skins would burst, the wine would spill, and the skins would be ruined. Instead, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”
While Jesus was saying this, a ruler came, bowed before him, and said, “My daughter has just died. But come and place your hand on her, and she’ll live.”
Jesus got up and followed him, and his disciples went too.
A woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of his robe.
She had been saying to herself, “If I can just touch his robe, I’ll be healed.”
Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take heart, daughter. Your faith has healed you.” The woman was healed at that moment.
When Jesus entered the ruler’s home, he saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
He said, “Go away. The girl isn’t dead; she’s sleeping.” They laughed at him.
After the crowd had been sent outside, Jesus went in, took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
News of this spread through the whole region.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting, “Son of David, have mercy on us!”
When Jesus went into a house, the blind men came to him. He asked them, “Do you believe I can do this?” They replied, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen for you according to your faith.”
Their eyes were opened. Jesus firmly warned them, “Make sure no one hears about this.”
But they went out and spread the news about him throughout that region.
As they were leaving, some people brought Jesus a man who couldn’t speak because he was possessed by a demon.
When Jesus drove the demon out, the man began speaking. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever happened in Israel!”
But the Pharisees said, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
Jesus traveled through all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, announcing the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
When he saw the crowds, he felt deep compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he told his disciples, “The harvest is huge, but the workers are few.
So ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into his harvest.”
